claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is primarily controlled by local chemical inhomogeneities.
The local chemical inhomogeneities develop through differential elemental diffusion during cooling.
Cr and Al are relatively slow-diffusing species in this alloy.
Cr and Al segregate into specific regions during moderate cooling or isothermal exposure.
Local Cr/Al segregation lowers the nucleation barrier for ordered or secondary phases.
Possible secondary products include B2- or L1₀-type structures formed from the high-temperature BCC matrix.
The proposed initial material is homogenized, single-phase BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
A rapid quench can retain a mostly single-phase BCC state with minimal secondary phases or compositional segregation.
An approximately 500 °C hold for 12–24 hours permits sufficient diffusion to generate local segregation.
Cr/Al-enriched regions have an enhanced thermodynamic driving force for ordered-phase formation.
The compositionally enriched regions promote heterogeneous nucleation of secondary phases.
Relative to rapid quenching, slower cooling or an intermediate isothermal hold will produce localized secondary phases.
Secondary phases will spatially correlate with Cr/Al-enriched regions.
The secondary-phase volume fraction will increase with longer hold times.
The secondary-phase volume fraction will increase as cooling becomes slower.
The proposed mechanism applies in intermediate-temperature regimes around 500 °C where diffusion remains active.
The proposed mechanism should not operate during sufficiently rapid cooling because diffusion is effectively frozen.
The kinetically controlled mechanism should cease to apply after exposures long enough to cause full homogenization or complete phase transformation.

contradictions.description: The material is described as a high-temperature BCC matrix, but the initial-state field says that this BCC state is obtained by solution treatment 'above the BCC stability range.' Read literally, treatment above the stability range would not yield equilibrium BCC; the intended solution-treatment temperature relative to the BCC range needs clarification.
